text: Some clients need to pay a deposit before we hold a visit for them. Here's how to ask for one by text or email, and how it's used at the visit.
When you open the visit of a client who needs a deposit,
the client alerts say Deposit required, right at the top, and how to collect it.
A deposit is real money. It's held on the account for this visit, then used at checkout.
Right-click the visit.
Then Client.
And Appointment Deposit.
It starts at a hundred dollars. Change it if the visit needs more.
The window reminds you how the deposit is used.
Click Text pay link. It sends a secure link for just the deposit.
You can change the wording before you send it.
Click Send message.
Scout shows the deposit is asked for, and what's still to collect.
Email pay link does the same by email.
If they're on the phone with a card, or paying cash, use Take payment now.
When Tom pays the link, the deposit shows on his Billing tab as its own bill, with no charges.
Until the visit, it's held for Biscuit's visit. Pay links for other bills, the online store and account credit on other bills leave it alone.
At checkout, click Account credit.
Scout includes Biscuit's deposit and uses it first.
Click Apply credit.
The deposit came off the bill. Take the rest as usual.
If the client cancels, the deposit becomes ordinary account credit. Add the cancel fee to a bill and pay it with Account credit.
If they don't show, do the same, and tick the visit's deposit in the Account credit box to use it on the fee.
The most common mistake is charging the card at checkout and forgetting the deposit. Remember: a deposit is held for its visit, so use Account credit at checkout, or on the cancel fee.
